question: I sold my home in 2025. Do I still report the sale to CRA if it was my principal residence the whole time?
generated_answer: Yes, you still need to report the sale of your principal residence to the CRA, even if it was your principal residence for the entire time you owned it. This is because the CRA requires you to report all capital gains or losses from the sale of property, including your principal residence. However, if the property was your principal residence for the entire time you owned it, you may be eligible to claim the principal residence exemption, which would exempt the gain from tax. You would still need to report the sale on your tax return, but you would also need to complete Form T2091, Designation of a Property as a Principal Residence by an Individual (Other Than a Personal Trust), to claim the exemption. It's always a good idea to consult with a tax professional to ensure you're meeting all your tax obligations correctly.
